sections.html:
Scientific name: Pareiorhaphis steindachneri (Miranda Ribeiro, 1918)

Type locality: Rio Itapucú, Santa Catharina, Brazil.

Size: 124 mm (4.9 in) SL.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2018).
Family: Loricariidae. Size: 14.5 cm. Temperature: 22-26°C. pH: 6.0-7.5. Common name: none. Specific name steindachneri honours Franz Steindachner, the Austrian ichthyologist (1834-1919).
South America: Brazil. Rivers of Santa Catarina State: Cubatão, Tubarão and Araranguá.
South America: Cubatão, Itapocu, and Itajaí-Açu River basins in Brazil, in the states of Paraná and Santa Catarina. Type locality: Flum. Rio Itapucú (Santa Catharina) [Brazil].

A frequent and abundant species that inhabits fast-flowing, well-oxygenated, cold waters with rocky substrates and preserved vegetation cover. It is found under rocks in fast flowing waters. In parts of its range there are threats such as deforestation, mining, and pollution from pesticides, but these do not represent a risk of extinction. The species occurs in several conservation units (e.g., Serra de Itajaí National Park) and is categorised as Least Concern (LC) (IUCN 2022).
Temperature 22-26°C, pH 6.0-7.5. Will need a good water flow in the aquarium.

Pareiorhaphis species are primarily diagnosed from remaining neoplecostomines by having the canal plate firmly articulated to the preopercle, and by a series of sexually-dimorphic features of hypertrophied odontodes of adult males, giving the fish a hispid appearance.

Pectoral fin overlapping half the length of pelvic fin; absence of a skin flap on dorsal margin of the pectoral-fin spine; nuptial males with pectoral-fin spines thick, straight and richly ornamented with short hypertrophied odontodes.

Description: dorsal spines (total): 1; dorsal soft rays (total): 7; anal soft rays: 6. Preadipose azygous plates 1-2; hypertrophied odontodes on head margins longer than mandibular ramus and shorter than snout length in fully mature males; cleithral width 27.9-33.7% SL; adipose fin present; pectoral fin spine curved and short, not passing half of pelvic fin when adpressed; head length 30.2-36.4% SL.
Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Sciências (Rio de Janeiro) v. 2, pp 107.
